name: Limitation of liability cap
text: Each party's total aggregate liability under the agreement must be capped at a fixed multiple of the fees paid or payable in the preceding 12 months.
preferred: Mutual cap equal to 12 months of fees paid or payable, with no carve-outs beyond those required by law.
fallback: Cap of no less than 6 months of fees, or a fixed monetary amount agreed in advance.
variants: Neither party's total liability arising out of this agreement shall exceed the amounts paid by the customer in the twelve months before the claim.
Aggregate liability is limited to a stated sum and the supplier is not liable for damages above that cap.
The maximum liability of either party for all claims is limited to the charges paid under this agreement.

name: Exclusion of consequential damages
text: Neither party may be liable for indirect, incidental, special or consequential damages, including loss of profit, revenue or goodwill.
preferred: Mutual exclusion of indirect and consequential loss, including lost profits and loss of data.
fallback: Exclusion applies to the supplier only where the customer's own exposure is also limited.
variants: In no event shall either party be liable for lost profits, loss of revenue, or any indirect or consequential loss.
Neither party will be responsible for special, punitive or incidental damages however caused.
Liability for loss of business, anticipated savings or goodwill is excluded.

name: Uncapped liability carve-outs
text: The liability cap must not apply to death or personal injury caused by negligence, fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, data breach or indemnified IP claims.
preferred: Cap excludes fraud, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, confidentiality breach and indemnity obligations.
fallback: Super-cap of 3 times annual fees for data protection and confidentiality breaches.
variants: Nothing in this agreement limits liability for fraud, death or personal injury, or wilful misconduct.
The limitations above do not apply to a party's indemnification obligations or breach of confidentiality.
Exclusions from the liability cap include gross negligence and breach of data protection obligations.

name: IP infringement indemnity
text: The supplier must defend and indemnify the customer against third-party claims that the services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
preferred: Supplier indemnifies, defends and holds harmless the customer against third-party IP infringement claims, with uncapped liability.
fallback: Indemnity limited to claims in the customer's territory, with a right for the supplier to procure, modify or replace.
variants: Supplier shall indemnify and hold harmless the customer from any claim that the services infringe a patent, copyright or trade secret.
The provider will defend the client against allegations that use of the deliverables violates third-party intellectual property rights.
Each party agrees to indemnify the other for losses arising from third-party infringement claims.

name: Mutual indemnification and procedure
text: Indemnities must be reasonable and mutual, covering third-party claims arising from breach, negligence or violation of law, with prompt notice, control of the defence and cooperation.
preferred: Mutual indemnities for third-party claims arising from breach of law or negligence, with notice, control of defence and no settlement without consent.
fallback: One-way indemnity from the supplier acceptable if limited to third-party claims.
variants: The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice and allow the indemnifying party to control the defence and settlement.
The customer shall indemnify the supplier against all losses, liabilities and costs arising from the customer's use of the services.
Each party shall indemnify the other against third-party claims arising from its negligence or breach of applicable law.

name: Termination for convenience and notice
text: The customer must be able to terminate for convenience on no more than 30 days' written notice, without early termination fees.
preferred: Either party may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice; customer pays only for services rendered.
fallback: Termination for convenience after the initial term on 90 days' notice.
variants: Either party may terminate this agreement at any time by giving thirty days' written notice to the other.
The agreement renews automatically for successive terms unless a party gives notice of non-renewal before the end of the current term.
The customer may end the agreement early upon payment of the remaining fees for the committed term.

name: Termination for cause and cure period
text: Either party may terminate for material breach that remains uncured 30 days after written notice, or immediately upon insolvency.
preferred: Mutual termination right for uncured material breach after 30 days' notice and for insolvency, with refund of prepaid fees.
fallback: Cure period of no less than 15 days.
variants: If either party commits a material breach and fails to remedy it within thirty days of notice, the other may terminate.
This agreement may be terminated immediately if the other party becomes insolvent or enters bankruptcy proceedings.
Upon termination for the supplier's breach, the customer is entitled to a pro rata refund of prepaid fees.

name: Payment terms and late fees
text: Invoices must be payable within 30 days of receipt of a valid invoice; late interest must not exceed 1% per month and disputed amounts may be withheld in good faith.
preferred: Net 45 payment terms, right to withhold disputed amounts, and no late fee on amounts disputed in good faith.
fallback: Net 30 payment terms with late interest capped at 1% per month.
variants: The customer shall pay each invoice within thirty days of the invoice date.
Overdue amounts accrue interest at 1.5% per month until paid in full.
Fees are non-refundable and payable in advance; the supplier may suspend the services for non-payment.

name: Fee increases and price protection
text: The supplier may not increase fees during the initial term, and later increases must be capped (for example CPI or 5%) with at least 60 days' notice.
preferred: Fees fixed for the initial term; renewal increases capped at the lower of CPI or 3%, on 90 days' notice.
fallback: Annual increases capped at 7% with 60 days' notice.
variants: The supplier may adjust its fees on notice to the customer.
Fees will increase annually by the percentage increase in the consumer price index.
Prices are fixed for the initial term and may be revised on renewal subject to prior written notice.

name: Data protection and security
text: The supplier must process personal data only on documented instructions, maintain appropriate security measures, use sub-processors only with approval, notify breaches within 72 hours and delete or return data on termination.
preferred: DPA on the customer's template: instructions-only processing, security standards (SOC 2 or ISO 27001), sub-processor approval, breach notice within 48 hours.
fallback: Supplier DPA acceptable if it meets GDPR Article 28 requirements and gives 72-hour breach notice.
variants: The processor shall process personal data only on the written instructions of the controller and implement appropriate technical and organisational measures.
The supplier shall notify the customer without undue delay, and in any event within 72 hours, of becoming aware of a personal data breach.
Upon termination the supplier shall delete or return all customer data and certify deletion in writing.

name: Intellectual property ownership
text: The customer must own its data and all deliverables created specifically for it; the supplier retains its pre-existing IP and grants the customer a licence to use embedded materials.
preferred: Customer owns all custom deliverables and customer data; supplier retains pre-existing IP and grants a perpetual, royalty-free licence to embedded materials.
fallback: Supplier owns deliverables but grants the customer an exclusive, perpetual, irrevocable licence.
variants: All intellectual property rights in the deliverables shall vest in the customer upon payment.
The supplier retains all right, title and interest in the services, software and any improvements, and grants the customer a limited licence to use them.
Each party retains ownership of its pre-existing materials; customer data remains the exclusive property of the customer.

name: Confidentiality obligations
text: Both parties must keep the other's confidential information secret, use it only for the agreement, and the obligation must survive termination for at least 3 years with standard exceptions.
preferred: Mutual confidentiality, use limited to performance of the agreement, 5-year survival (trade secrets indefinitely), standard exclusions and compelled-disclosure carve-out.
fallback: 3-year survival with return or destruction of materials on request.
variants: Each party shall hold the other's confidential information in strict confidence and not disclose it to any third party.
The obligations of confidentiality survive for five years after termination of the agreement.
Confidential information does not include information that is public, independently developed, or lawfully received from a third party.

name: Governing law and jurisdiction
text: The agreement must be governed by the law of an agreed neutral or home jurisdiction, with disputes resolved in the courts or by arbitration seated in that jurisdiction.
preferred: Governed by the law of the customer's home jurisdiction, with exclusive jurisdiction of its courts.
fallback: Neutral law (England and Wales or New York) with arbitration seated in a neutral city.
variants: This agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of England and Wales.
The parties submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the supplier's home country.
Any dispute arising under this agreement shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration.

name: Service levels and remedies
text: The supplier must meet defined uptime and support response commitments, with service credits and a termination right for repeated failure.
preferred: 99.9% monthly uptime, defined response times, service credits of up to 25% of monthly fees, and termination right after repeated misses.
fallback: 99.5% uptime with service credits as the sole remedy for minor misses.
variants: The supplier shall make the services available at least 99.9% of the time in each calendar month.
If availability falls below the target, the customer is entitled to service credits against future invoices.
The supplier will perform the services with reasonable skill and care and in accordance with the specification.
